rule: A symbol map is absolute-linked when the load base is positive and the map's lowest text symbol sits at or above it. Subtracting a base from such a map shifts every frame onto an unrelated function, which resolves to a plausible name rather than to an error.
why_shared: Three runtimes implement this rule: scripts/resolve-backtrace.sh, scripts/telemetry-crashes.py and server/crash-worker/src/symbol-resolver.ts. They cannot share code, so they share this table and each has a conformance test over it. Change the rule here and all three go red together.

cases.name: PIE image: symbols linked near zero, device reports its mapping address
non-PIE static image: lowest text symbol is exactly the reported base
non-PIE static image: lowest text symbol sits above the reported base
boundary: one byte below the base is still relative
no base reported: nothing to subtract, so the question does not arise
empty symbol map: no lowest symbol to judge by
